Hopeless? Despairing? You might be an extremist, according to the government.

Shortly before the midterm election, "national security" decided that being
pessimistic made you a domestic terrorist.

They called it "Eco-Nihilist/Anti-Human Extremism." It's even got an acronym:
ENAH.

The government says that ENAH is "an ideological movement that combines
extreme environmental beliefs with the view that humanity itself is
fundamentally harmful to the planet."

Not only is this graduate school crap, invented by some state-level "analyst"
to describe an America that he/she doesn't understand, but it is the product
of a runaway system that manufactures domestic threats like candy.

So while the American public showed up last week to resoundingly announce that
it _did_ care about the state of the country, the world, and the future of the
planet, that very public Tsunami is about to meet a grinding seawall of
negativism that is dedicated to thwarting their very demand for change.

This threat machine has worked over the past two years to stigmatize
immigrants, Gaza protestors, "Antifa," those who are LGBTQ+, Somali-Americans,
and those who are "anti-Christian," "anti-capital" or "anti-American" as
"threats" to America. And it continues, despite the epic demonstration of
democracy and life-affirmation.

* * *

The government's legacy of attacking domestic discontent (and democracy
itself) goes back to the days of J. Edgar Hoover. Of course there were Soviet-
inspired communists. And there were internal threats to the State, like Puerto
Rican nationalists who even attacked the Capitol in 1954. But on the other
hand, there was also Martin Luther King Jr. and John Lennon, and a host of
other Americans who were never criminals of any kind and who the threat
machine sought to destroy.

Now, the Trump administration has designated the "left" and "socialism" and
anyone who is "anti-American" as potential terrorists. And though there have
also been time periods when right wing white nationalists or self-declared
"militias" were also in the government's sights, mostly this domestic security
apparatus has gone after the "left" (or whatever it is that they define as the
left). It is a gift that keeps on giving, especially in the post-9/11 period
when the priority for these agencies is catching terrorists before they strike
and even before they break the law.

To the internal security agencies, this means translating everything from
innocent associations to free speech into "indicators" of potential
lawlessness. The ENAH report -- labeled "For Official Use Only/Law Enforcement
Sensitive" -- describes an "ideological movement" that clearly doesn't exist.
It was prepared by the Minnesota Fusion Center, and is circulating throughout
the country in homeland security channels.

The government says that it has newly invented the ENAH category for "threat
recognition." The "movement" could "contribute to the radicalization of
isolated individuals," it says. "Adherents may argue that environmental
degradation and climate change can only be resolved through a drastic
reduction in the human population or the collapse of modern civilization," it
continues.

Thus those who are concerned about climate change are treated as if they are
an adjunct of _al Qaeda_ , an army of brainwashed malcontents who care nothing
about society and represent some threat not just to the American way of life
but to western civilization.

Though in one place the report says that ENAH is an "ideological movement," in
the fine print it goes on to say that it isn't a movement at all. "While ENAH
ideas have appeared in isolated writings, online communities, and extremist
manifestos, they do not represent a cohesive, organized movement," the report
reads. "The ideology often overlaps with misanthropy, accelerationism, or
apocalyptic worldviews, emphasizing despair rather than constructive
environmental solutions."

Which is it? And this is supposed to be an "intelligence" assessment of
threats to America?

So, you're worried? That gets turned into the potential for arson or rioting.
You think overpopulation is an issue? That's the equivalent of being part of a
movement to "advocate or carry out indiscriminate violence against people."
Concerned about data centers? That becomes "anti-technology violent extremism"
and a "threat" to "critical infrastructure."

And all of that becomes the predicate for investigating and spying on the
public at large.

The Minnesota report points to a single citizen as proof that this latest
category of Eco-Nihilist/Anti-Human extremism exists and is a pressing threat:
the suicide bombing by Guy Bartkus in 2025 outside of a fertility clinic in
Palm Springs, California. Bartkus, the report says: "left writings expressing
anti-natalist and anti-human views, arguing that bringing new people into
existence was immoral."

The FBI's assistant director in charge of the Los Angeles Field Office
[told](https://edition.cnn.com/2025/05/19/us/guy-bartkus-palm-springs-bombing-
suspect-wwk) the press that "The subject had nihilistic ideations." Retired
senior FBI profiler Dr. Mary Ellen O'Toole jumped in to tell CNN that this
ideation involved a "preoccupation with themes of violence, hopelessness,
despair, pessimism, hatred, isolation, loneliness, or an 'end-of-the-world'
philosophy."

Now that "anti-human extremism" has been created as a category of Americans
who need to be policed, the Bureau and other agencies think they are justified
to look at forum posts, social media discussions, and chat rooms for threats.
Nowhere in the Bartkus case is there any effort to explain how he (or anyone
like him) threatens "America." The specific words he wrote down before he died
is the evidence, and it is the justification to come to the conclusion that
there are other Bartkus's out there ready to strike.

On that note, the Minnesota report concludes with an explicit acknowledgement
that it's all fantasy:

> "... ENAH violence is _extremely uncommon_ but could potentially have high
> impact. Most violent cases would likely involve lone actors or very small
> online networks rather than organized groups, and the MNFC [Minnesota fusion
> center] notes that these beliefs often overlap with nihilism,
> accelerationism, or other violent extremist ideologies rather than existing
> as a standalone movement."

ENAH is part of an even broader and vaguer category of Nihilistic Violent
Extremism (NVE) which was supercharged last year. "Law enforcement has
increasingly used the analytical label Nihilistic Violent Extremism (NVE) for
a small number of cases in which offenders espouse generalized hatred of
society or humanity instead of traditional ideological goals," the report
says.

"A generalized hatred of society"? Doesn't that describe every young person
from the beginning of Rock n'Roll to the present?

By now it should become clear that the people conceptualizing, writing,
editing and approving this report know nothing. That is because no one in any
fusion center, not at homeland security, in the FBI, or the intelligence
world, or in all of national security is an expert on America -- what it
means, what makes it tick, what actually threatens the country, or indeed what
terrorizes the people.

In the counterterrorism world, the internal threat is not just vague but
shockingly ill-defined. As a result, the government can get away with labeling
Luigi Mangione or Alex Pretti or Renee Good as terrorists. The FBI might
officially [say](https://www.fbi.gov/news/speeches-and-testimony/oversight-of-
the-federal-bureau-of-investigation-061021) that it does not investigate First
Amendment-protected speech, peaceful protests, or political activity, but in
fact with the ENAH and NVE categorizations, it does. It just does so in the
name of countering "extremism" or terrorism.

Clearly this machine is wrong about who the American people are. But, despite
the outcome of the elections, it will continue to work in the background to
now attack elected Muslims and socialists and others, who even under Democrat
rule, they will continue to think are a threat to America.

So the question has to be asked: What does any "fusion" center, or the
Department of Homeland Security, or the FBI for that matter really know about
America and what threatens it? And when do we take their power to manufacture
these threats away?
